newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher despite Europe selloff.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher despite Europe selloff.

text.p: Taiwan stocks, seemingly immune to the week's big U.S. and European slides, closed higher on Wednesday on the heels of Tuesday's big rise, though late profit-taking on electronics erased some early gains.
The benchmark index ended up 40.48 points or 0.50 percent at 8,203.89, off an intraday high of 8,258.92.
Turnover was a brisk T$165.4 billion.

"Despite the big declines on Wall Street and the European markets, the domestic index rose again as investors entered the market to hunt for low-priced shares," said National Securities manager Allen Huang.

The overseas markets tumbled on likely interest rate hikes, a situation not expected in Taiwan where brokers said the central bank would not tighten liquidity for fear of hurting a local economic recovery, which remains frustratingly slow.

Late selling focused on electronics, which fell 1.09 percent after its recent rallies. Chipmaker United Microelectronics slid T$1.5 to T$54, though notebook computer maker Clevo rose T$6 to T$306 on its debut after switching from the small over-the-counter market.
Low-priced steel, paper and automobile shares surged 5.47, 4.78 and 4.56 percent, respectively.

"Electronics have been overheated recently, but if the sector enters consolidation for some time, it should emerge again as the bellwether sector because its earnings are still the best in Taiwan," said National's Huang.
Steel shares surged on recent steel price hikes and expectations of solid 1997 demand spurred by reported sales growth in the property and construction sectors, brokers said.
Giant China Steel rose the daily seven percent limit to T$28.3.
For Thursday, a 8,150-8,250 trading range was seen.
